target_customer: Hospitals, oncologists and radiologists who pay for automated measurement of CT and MRI scans
problem: Measuring tumor lesions, muscle and fat from routine scans is slow and manual for radiologists, so useful data in the scan goes unused.
business_model: B2B software licensed to hospitals and research groups (pricing not public)

founders.name: Angelica Iacovelli
education: BS and MS in Mathematical Engineering, Politecnico di Milano

founders.name: Luca Pegolotti
prior_employers: Stanford School of Medicine (PhD research and postdoc)

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable segmentation and RECIST style lesion measurement across scanners and hospitals needs clinical validation, and FDA clearance is still ahead (YC jobs page says building toward it).

defensibility.rationale: Clearance and hospital data partnerships could become a moat, but neither was confirmed as of the sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Nucleo found. A search review said only general clinical imaging AI platforms were comparable alternatives, without naming vendors.

market_need_then: Oncology imaging review is labor intensive; the company cites partnerships with Stanford, Cedars-Sinai, UCI Health and Weill Cornell as demand evidence (company claim).

identity.visual_style: 3D CT render with colored lesions on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical; tagline 'Intelligence for medical imaging', 'The data is already in the scan'

brand_strength.rationale: A search for brand coverage found nothing about the company's brand; the name is shared with unrelated Nucleo, Nucleus and NucleoBio entities.

outcome_analysis: Nucleo is an early stage Fall 2025 company with two research-heavy founders from Stanford, Apple and Politecnico di Milano, selling to hospitals. No funding round beyond YC, no exit and no shutdown were found. The main open risks are clinical validation, FDA clearance and slow hospital sales cycles.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: VCBacked lists 500K pre-seed with Y Combinator, Dealroom lists a 125K seed, Startup-Seeker says undisclosed. None is confirmed by a company or press source, so no round is recorded. The competitor search returned no dated competitors near the batch; the list is empty. The outcome search found nothing about the company. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked, Dec 2025, Y Combinator); Nordic 9 dates a 500K round to 2025-09-15, so the date conflicts; PitchBook shows 650K; no press or filing confirms. A 4M seed in 2022 belongs to a different company named Nucleo.
